Postcondition: the session identifier, remember-me series, refresh tokens, and channel-specific sessions are revoked, federated logout is propagated, and the response clears cookies with matching scope. Replaying any pre-logout credential fails, and cached pages are not restored without re-authentication.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-06: Complete Session Termination Invariant

rule_constraints.server: logout deletes the server-side session record
rule_constraints.tokens: all derived tokens and remember-me series revoked
rule_constraints.federation: identity provider logout invoked where applicable
rule_constraints.transport: logout requires POST with CSRF token

text: Security invariant: sessions expire server-side after a short idle period and an absolute maximum lifetime, regardless of client behavior. Precondition: a session exists. Postcondition: inactivity beyond the idle threshold invalidates the session, total age beyond the absolute cap invalidates it, and high-risk actions require fresh authentication. Expiry is enforced on every request, not by a client timer, and the user is informed before an interactive timeout.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-07: Bounded Session Lifetime Invariant

rule_constraints.idle: idle timeout <= 15 minutes for sensitive apps

text: Security invariant: session state is namespaced per module and flow, cleared when a flow completes, and never used as the authority for authorization decisions. Precondition: a flow writes state into the session. Postcondition: transient values are removed on completion, keys cannot collide across modules, and authorization derives roles and tenants from server-side records rather than mutable session flags. Every session value is revalidated at the point of use.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-08: Namespaced Immutable Session State Invariant

rule_constraints.lifecycle: clear transient state on flow completion and login
rule_constraints.authority: authorization reads server-side records, not session flags
rule_constraints.validation: session values revalidated at each use

text: Security invariant: session tokens are protected from script and network exposure, bound to contextual signals where feasible, rotated on risk, and monitored for concurrent use. Precondition: a session is established. Postcondition: tokens are unreadable by script and never sent in cleartext, anomalous context changes trigger re-authentication or revocation, concurrent distant sessions raise an alert, and the user can revoke all sessions. High-value actions require step-up even within a valid session.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-09: Context-Bound Session Invariant

rule_constraints.binding: token bound to device fingerprint or client certificate where feasible
rule_constraints.rotation: rotate on risk signals and periodically

text: Security invariant: every endpoint accepts only TLS 1.2 or 1.3 with AEAD cipher suites, a valid certificate, and strong key material, and clients validate the chain and hostname. Precondition: a client connects to a TLS endpoint. Postcondition: weak protocols and ciphers are not negotiated, certificates are verified, HSTS enforces HTTPS, and renegotiation is secure. Configuration is scanned continuously and drift raises an alert.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-01: Modern TLS-Only Invariant

rule_constraints.ciphers: AEAD suites only; no RC4, 3DES, NULL, or export
rule_constraints.certificate: valid chain, strong key, correct hostname, not expired
rule_constraints.validation: clients verify certificates and pin where appropriate

text: Security invariant: all encryption uses an AEAD mode or encrypt-then-MAC with a constant-time integrity check, and decryption failures are indistinguishable to the attacker. Precondition: the application encrypts or decrypts attacker-observable data. Postcondition: tampered ciphertext is rejected before plaintext is processed, padding and content errors return one uniform response, and timing does not depend on validity. Keys are managed centrally, IVs are random and unique, and legacy CBC code is migrated.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-02: Authenticated Encryption Invariant

rule_constraints.mode: AEAD such as AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305

text: Security invariant: every channel that carries credentials, personal data, tokens, or security-relevant telemetry uses authenticated TLS, including internal service-to-service traffic. Precondition: data classified as sensitive is transmitted. Postcondition: only TLS-protected channels are used, cleartext service ports are disabled or firewalled, certificates are validated, and payloads contain no secrets in URLs or logs. Channel inventory is maintained and new integrations are reviewed before deployment.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-03: Encrypted Channel Invariant for Sensitive Data

rule_constraints.channels: TLS for all external and internal sensitive traffic
rule_constraints.services: no cleartext SMTP, LDAP, SQL, or cache ports
rule_constraints.payloads: no secrets in URLs or logs

text: Security invariant: security-relevant cryptography uses vetted modern primitives with managed keys, random unique IVs, and authenticated modes. Precondition: the application hashes, encrypts, signs, or derives keys. Postcondition: passwords use Argon2id, bcrypt, or scrypt with per-user salts; integrity uses SHA-256 or better; encryption uses AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 with no ECB; keys live in a KMS and rotate. Home-grown schemes are prohibited, and cryptographic choices are reviewed against current guidance.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-04: Modern Cryptography Invariant

rule_constraints.hashing: SHA-256+ for integrity; Argon2id/bcrypt/scrypt for passwords

text: Security invariant: every reflected value is encoded for its exact output context, and client-side code never writes untrusted data into executable DOM sinks. Precondition: request data is rendered into a response. Postcondition: HTML body, attribute, URL, JavaScript, and CSS contexts each receive correct encoding, DOM sinks use textContent or a sanitizer, and CSP limits inline script. Framework auto-escaping is the default, and every explicit bypass is reviewed.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-01: Context-Aware Output Encoding Invariant

rule_constraints.encoding: HTML, attribute, URL, JS, and CSS encoders per sink
rule_constraints.dom: no untrusted data in innerHTML, document.write, or eval

text: Security invariant: persisted user content is sanitized with a maintained allowlist sanitizer and re-encoded for its render context, so no stored value can execute script. Precondition: user content is stored and later rendered. Postcondition: dangerous tags, attributes, and URL schemes are removed, rich text is sanitized on store and again on render, and every view uses context-aware encoding. CSP blocks inline script, and admin and support views receive the same treatment as public pages.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-02: Stored Content Sanitization Invariant

rule_constraints.sanitize: allowlist HTML sanitizer on input and output
rule_constraints.context: encode per sink at render time
rule_constraints.rich_text: sanitize on store and re-sanitize on render

text: Security invariant: authorization is enforced in the router for every HTTP method a route accepts, and each route explicitly declares its permitted methods. Precondition: a request targets any route. Postcondition: unauthorized requests fail regardless of verb, unlisted methods return 405, method override headers are disabled or restricted to trusted clients, and the same policy applies to HEAD and OPTIONS. Route tests exercise every method in CI.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-03: Method-Agnostic Authorization Invariant

rule_constraints.authorization: evaluated in the router for every method
rule_constraints.override: method override headers disabled or validated

text: Security invariant: every tier parses parameters identically, and duplicate or ambiguous names are rejected or canonicalized before any security decision. Precondition: a request carries parameters. Postcondition: only one value per name reaches the application, arrays are explicitly typed, encoded variants are normalized, and the WAF and origin share a parser or a normalized representation. Schemas reject unexpected multiplicity, and tests cover duplicate-name cases.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-04: Canonical Single-Value Parameter Invariant

rule_constraints.consistency: edge and origin use the same parser
rule_constraints.security: decisions use the canonical parsed value

text: Security invariant: all SQL values are bound through prepared statements, identifiers come from a fixed allowlist, and the database account holds only the privileges the feature needs. Precondition: a query includes user-influenced data. Postcondition: input never becomes syntax, dynamic identifiers resolve through a map, errors are generic, and ORM raw fragments are reviewed. Escaping is defense in depth only.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-05: Parameterized Query Invariant

text: Security invariant: every user value inserted into an LDAP filter is escaped per RFC 4515, or the directory API is used with parameter binding, and the service account has only the rights required. Precondition: a directory query includes user input. Postcondition: metacharacters cannot change filter logic, wildcard searches are explicit and authorized, errors are generic, and results are limited to the intended scope.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-06: Escaped LDAP Filter Invariant

rule_constraints.scope: bind with a least-privilege service account
rule_constraints.validation: reject control characters and overlong input

text: Security invariant: XML is constructed with a library that escapes text nodes and attributes, validated against a strict schema, and parsed with DTDs and external entities disabled. Precondition: user data enters an XML document. Postcondition: metacharacters cannot create elements, attributes, or comments, duplicate fields are rejected, and signatures cover canonicalized content. String concatenation is prohibited, and parsers enforce the schema before processing.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-07: Safe XML Construction Invariant

rule_constraints.construct: use an XML builder or DOM API, not string concatenation

text: Security invariant: server-side includes are disabled everywhere untrusted content can be written or reflected, and directive syntax is escaped in any user-visible output. Precondition: user content is stored or rendered by the web server. Postcondition: no path containing user content has SSI processing enabled, upload directories do not map to SSI handlers, and server configuration is audited for Includes options.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-08: SSI Disabled for Untrusted Content Invariant

rule_constraints.ssi: disabled on upload and user-content paths
rule_constraints.handler: no SSI mapping for user extensions
rule_constraints.encoding: escape directive syntax in reflected content
rule_constraints.review: server config audited for Options Includes

text: Security invariant: XPath queries use variables or an API that binds values, never string concatenation, and errors do not reveal the expression. Precondition: user input is used in an XPath query. Postcondition: quotes, brackets, and boolean operators cannot change the predicate, the queried node set is limited to the intended scope, and failures are indistinguishable.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-09: Parameterized XPath Invariant

rule_constraints.escape: escape quotes and brackets if concatenation is unavoidable
rule_constraints.scope: limit the queried document and node set

text: Security invariant: mail commands are built through a protocol library with structured fields, and addresses and headers reject CR, LF, and NUL characters. Precondition: user input influences an SMTP or IMAP command. Postcondition: input cannot terminate a command or add a header, recipients are strictly parsed, outbound volume per account is limited, and the server refuses relay to unauthorized domains.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-10: Protocol-Safe Mail Command Invariant

rule_constraints.crlf: reject CR, LF, and NUL in addresses and headers
rule_constraints.api: use a mail library with structured fields

text: Security invariant: untrusted input is never evaluated as code and never controls an include path; resource selection uses a fixed server-side map. Precondition: a feature evaluates expressions or loads files dynamically. Postcondition: eval and equivalent constructs are absent from request paths, include targets come from an allowlist of identifiers, remote and filter wrappers are disabled, and uploaded files cannot be executed. Errors are generic and execution runs under least privilege.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-11: No-Dynamic-Evaluation Invariant

rule_constraints.eval: no eval, assert, or dynamic code from input
rule_constraints.include: paths from a fixed map, never from request data
rule_constraints.upload: uploaded files never reachable by the interpreter

text: Security invariant: external commands are invoked through an argument-array API with shell interpretation disabled, and every user-influenced argument is allowlisted or strongly typed. Precondition: the application invokes an external program. Postcondition: metacharacters have no special meaning, leading dashes cannot inject options, library equivalents replace shell commands where possible, and execution runs under a dedicated low-privilege account with bounded output.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-12: Structured Command Execution Invariant

rule_constraints.validation: strict allowlist or strong typing per argument

text: Security invariant: format strings are constant literals and user data is always passed as an argument, never as the format itself. Precondition: a printf-family or logging API processes user data. Postcondition: conversion specifiers in input are inert, logging uses parameterized calls, and compiler format warnings are enabled and treated as errors. Localization and template formats validate specifiers before use.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-13: Fixed Format String Invariant

rule_constraints.format: constant format literal, input always an argument
rule_constraints.validation: reject or escape % in user-visible format contexts

text: Security invariant: stored data is revalidated and context-encoded at every point of use, regardless of the validation performed at entry. Precondition: data crosses a component, job, or time boundary. Postcondition: each consumer applies its own schema, type, and encoding controls, background jobs treat stored data as untrusted, and provenance and classification travel with the data. Entry validation is defense in depth, never a substitute for sink protection.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-14: Revalidate-at-Use Invariant

rule_constraints.trust: no stored data is trusted by default
rule_constraints.validate: schema and type checks at each consumer
rule_constraints.provenance: data classified at entry and on read

text: Security invariant: every hop in the chain uses a strict, consistent HTTP parser that rejects ambiguous framing and never reflects CRLF into headers. Precondition: a request or response traverses a proxy, load balancer, or origin. Postcondition: messages with conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding, duplicate framing headers, obs-fold, or CRLF in values are rejected, and all hops share the same normalization rules. Back-end connections are not reused across trust boundaries when framing is uncertain.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-15: Strict HTTP Framing Invariant

rule_constraints.framing: reject ambiguous Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding combinations
rule_constraints.crlf: reject CR and LF in header values
rule_constraints.headers: reject duplicate or obfuscated framing headers
rule_constraints.hops: consistent parser configuration across the chain

text: Security invariant: the server accepts only the request forms and methods its role requires, rejects absolute-form targets and CONNECT unless it is a deliberate proxy, and cannot originate traffic to internal ranges. Precondition: an HTTP request arrives at the web tier. Postcondition: unexpected forms and methods return 400 or 405, proxy headers are ignored, and egress policy prevents the web tier from reaching internal services. Request parsing is reviewed whenever a proxy or gateway is introduced.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-16: Explicit Request Surface Invariant

rule_constraints.egress: block server-originated traffic to internal ranges

text: Security invariant: absolute URLs and virtual-host routing derive from a configured canonical origin, and the Host header is validated against an allowlist before any use. Precondition: a request supplies Host or forwarding headers. Postcondition: unknown hosts are rejected or served a default, reset and notification links use the configured origin, and X-Forwarded-Host is honored only from a trusted proxy. Cache keys include the canonical host.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-17: Configured Canonical Host Invariant

rule_constraints.url: build absolute URLs from configured canonical origin
rule_constraints.forward: ignore X-Forwarded-Host unless from a trusted proxy

text: Security invariant: templates are authored by developers and user input is passed only as data variables, never concatenated into template source. Precondition: a feature renders a template with user-influenced values. Postcondition: expressions in input are inert, preview and email builders use predefined templates, and any dynamic template feature is sandboxed with a restricted context. The template engine is reviewed for reachable gadget objects.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-18: Template Data Separation Invariant

rule_constraints.render: templates are static; user data passed as variables

text: Security invariant: server-side fetches are restricted to an explicit allowlist and validated against the resolved IP after DNS resolution, with every redirect hop revalidated. Precondition: the server fetches a URL influenced by an external actor. Postcondition: private, loopback, link-local, and metadata ranges are unreachable, DNS rebinding is defeated by address pinning, egress policy enforces the same boundary, and responses are bounded and never returned raw.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-19: Resolved-Destination Invariant

rule_constraints.resolve: validate the resolved IP, not the string

text: Security invariant: a session is created only from a token that the server validates directly with the identity provider, and the session subject is the verified subject claim rather than any value supplied by the browser. Precondition: a user completes an OAuth login. Postcondition: the authorization code is exchanged back-channel, the signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and nonce are verified, the code is single-use, and the email or username in the request body is ignored. Implicit flow is disabled in favour of authorization code with PKCE.

metadata.title: OAuth Implicit Flow Authentication Bypass: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.flow: authorization code with PKCE; implicit flow disabled
rule_constraints.validation: verify signature, iss, aud, exp, and nonce server-side
rule_constraints.binding: session subject comes from the verified token, never a request body
rule_constraints.replay: single-use code, short-lived tokens, nonce checked

text: Security invariant: every OAuth linking and unlinking operation requires an unguessable state value bound to the authenticated session, and the operation is confirmed with fresh authentication. Precondition: a user initiates or completes an identity link. Postcondition: a request that does not carry the matching single-use state is rejected, the flow cannot be completed by a different session, the account owner receives a notification, and unlinking is equally protected. Linking a social identity is treated as a credential change, not a preference update.

metadata.title: Forced OAuth Profile Linking: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.state: cryptographic state bound to the session, single-use
rule_constraints.notify: email notification on identity link and unlink
rule_constraints.scope: linking and unlinking require the current password or MFA

text: Security invariant: redirect_uri must exactly match a pre-registered value and the authorization code is bound to that value, the client, and a PKCE verifier. Precondition: a client starts an authorization request. Postcondition: any redirect_uri with extra segments, encoded traversal, or a different host is rejected before the code is issued, the code is single-use and short-lived, and exchange fails unless the verifier and exact redirect match. Open redirects on the client are treated as an OAuth-critical defect.

metadata.title: OAuth Account Hijacking via redirect_uri: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.redirect: exact string match against registered URIs; no wildcards or traversal
rule_constraints.binding: authorization code bound to client and exact redirect_uri

text: Security invariant: access tokens never travel in a URL that can be redirected, and the client exposes no open redirect that could receive one. Precondition: an OAuth flow completes. Postcondition: the authorization code flow with PKCE replaces implicit flow, tokens are returned only to the exact registered callback over a back channel or fragment that cannot be forwarded, redirect destinations are allowlisted, and tokens have a narrow audience and short lifetime. Any open redirect is treated as an OAuth compromise primitive.

metadata.title: OAuth Access Token Theft via Open Redirect: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.redirect: no open redirect on the client; destination allowlist
rule_constraints.tokens: authorization code flow; tokens never in URLs
rule_constraints.fragment: token delivered only to the exact registered callback
rule_constraints.binding: token audience restricted to the client API

associated_labs: OAuth Access Token Theft via Open Redirect

text: Security invariant: cross-origin messages carrying credentials are sent only to an explicit trusted origin, and every listener validates event.origin before acting. Precondition: a page uses postMessage or can be framed. Postcondition: the target origin is never a wildcard for sensitive data, listeners reject messages from unknown origins, authentication pages set frame-ancestors to none, and tokens never appear in the URL of a page that can be embedded. Token-bearing pages are excluded from third-party framing entirely.

metadata.title: OAuth Access Token Theft via a Proxy Page: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.origin: postMessage targetOrigin is an explicit trusted origin
rule_constraints.framing: frame-ancestors restricts embedding of auth pages
rule_constraints.token: tokens never placed in a framable page URL

associated_labs: OAuth Access Token Theft via a Proxy Page

text: Security invariant: no claim from a JWT is read until the signature has been verified with a pinned algorithm and a trusted key, and the issuer, audience, expiry, and not-before claims are validated. Precondition: a request presents a JWT. Postcondition: a token with an invalid, missing, or unexpected signature is rejected before any authorization decision, verification uses strict library mode rather than decode-only helpers, and failures return a generic 401. Tests assert that a tampered payload is rejected.

metadata.title: JWT Unverified Signature Bypass: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.verify: every JWT is signature-verified before any claim is read
rule_constraints.library: strict verification mode with algorithms pinned
rule_constraints.claims: iss, aud, exp, and nbf validated
rule_constraints.fail: verification failure returns 401 without partial processing

text: Security invariant: the verification algorithm is chosen by the server and pinned per key, and the alg header in the token can never select or disable verification. Precondition: a JWT is presented. Postcondition: none and any unexpected algorithm are rejected unconditionally, an empty signature fails, and the library is called with an explicit expected algorithm. Case variants and whitespace in the header do not alter the decision, and tests cover alg=none submissions.

metadata.title: JWT alg=none Acceptance: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.algorithm: server pins the expected algorithm; header alg ignored
rule_constraints.signature: empty signature segment is a hard failure
rule_constraints.library: verification API that requires an explicit algorithm

text: Security invariant: JWT signing keys have at least 256 bits of entropy, live in a managed secret store, rotate on a schedule, and are never shared between environments or embedded in source. Precondition: a service signs or verifies tokens. Postcondition: HMAC secrets are generated with a CSPRNG, asymmetric keys are preferred for multi-service identity, key identifiers allow rotation without invalidating all sessions, and exposure triggers immediate revocation. Key strength is checked during provisioning.

metadata.title: JWT Weak Signing Key: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.entropy: HMAC secret >= 256 bits from a CSPRNG
rule_constraints.storage: secret in a KMS or secret manager, never in source

text: Security invariant: verification keys come only from a server-side trusted key store selected by a validated key identifier, and key material embedded in the token is never trusted. Precondition: a JWT with a key header is presented. Postcondition: jwk and jku headers are ignored or rejected, kid is matched against a fixed map, the algorithm is pinned per key, and a token that supplies its own key fails verification. Key rotation uses published JWKS from a trusted origin.

metadata.title: JWT jwk Header Injection: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.key: verification keys resolved only from a server-side trusted store
rule_constraints.jwk: jwk and jku headers ignored or rejected
rule_constraints.kid: kid maps to a known key, never to key material

text: Security invariant: remote key sets are fetched only from a fixed allowlist of trusted HTTPS origins, never from a URL chosen by the token, and retrieval fails closed. Precondition: a JWT references a remote key set. Postcondition: jku values outside the allowlist are rejected before any request, redirects are not followed, TLS is verified, responses are size-bounded, and keys are cached per issuer so a hostile set cannot contaminate other tenants. Enforcement belongs in a shared server-side control that every channel and endpoint traverses, backed by database constraints and persistent audit records rather than by the user interface or a single controller. Any missing or unparseable value must fail closed.

metadata.title: CWE-1390 Security Invariant: Proof Proportional to Privilege

rule_constraints.invariant: the authentication ceremony provides proof proportional to the privilege, with high-entropy factors, replay resistance, and recovery paths that cannot bypass the factor
rule_constraints.precondition: an identity claim is verified by one or more authentication factors
rule_constraints.postcondition: the factor cannot be guessed, replayed, or recovered through weaker secondary data, and privileged actions require a ceremony appropriate to their impact

text: Security invariant: an OTP is compared server-side and is never echoed, logged, or returned in any response, and the verified phone number is bound to the order session so later request fields cannot replace it. Precondition: the order workflow requires phone verification before placement. Postcondition: the order is accepted only when the submitted code matches the server-stored hash for the same normalized number, has not expired, and has not been consumed; the number used for fulfilment is the verified one, not a value re-read from the final request. Errors return a stable code and generic message.

metadata.title: Order Verification Invariant: No Secret Disclosure and Bound Phone Numbers
metadata.report_title: Bypass OTP verification when placing Order

rule_constraints.invariant: otp never returned to client and order.phone == verified_phone and hash_equals(stored, submitted)
rule_constraints.precondition: order placement requires verification of the contact number
rule_constraints.postcondition: accept the order only for the verified number and a single-use unexpired code; never echo the expected value

text: Security invariant: every order line is validated against the catalog's purchase limit on the server at cart submission and again at payment initiation, independent of any URL or client state. Precondition: the cart references a purchasable item with a per-order maximum. Postcondition: reject the order when quantity < 1, quantity > item.max_per_order, or the item is not in the active catalog, and bind the accepted quantities to a server-side cart identifier that the client cannot rewrite. Enforcement must sit in the order service, not in the storefront presentation layer.

metadata.title: Purchase Limit Invariant at the Checkout and Payment Boundary
metadata.report_title: [spectacles.com] Bypassing quantity limit in orders

rule_constraints.invariant: 1 <= quantity <= item.max_per_order for every order line at submission and at payment
rule_constraints.precondition: cart references an item with a defined per-order maximum
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject over-limit or non-integer quantities and bind accepted lines to a server-side cart id

text: Security invariant: order quantity is a positive integer bounded by the menu item's serving limits, and the payable total is recomputed server-side from the validated line items and the catalog price. Precondition: an order contains at least one menu item with a unit price. Postcondition: reject quantities that are non-integer, below one, negative, or above the item maximum; the charged amount equals the recomputed total and never falls below the price of a single serving. The cart and order endpoints must use the same validation routine.

metadata.title: Quantity Integrality and Server-Side Total Recomputation
metadata.report_title: [www.zomato.com] Tampering with Order Quantity and paying less amount then actual amount, leads to business loss

rule_constraints.invariant: quantity is an integer in [1, item.max] and total == sum(validated_quantity * catalog_price)
rule_constraints.precondition: an order contains menu items with catalog prices
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject fractional, zero, negative, or over-limit quantities and charge the recomputed total

text: Security invariant: seat quantity and price are resolved independently on the server from the add-on catalog, and the order total is recomputed from those values before checkout. Precondition: an order contains a ticketed add-on with a per-seat price. Postcondition: reject requests where the submitted count exceeds availability, is non-integer or negative, or where the submitted total differs from quantity * catalog_price; never accept a composite field that carries price information from the client. Availability must be decremented atomically with order creation.

metadata.title: Add-On Pricing Invariant and Server-Side Seat Validation
metadata.report_title: attacker can book unlimited tickets in free at https://aaf.com/checkout/order-received/21237/?key=wc_order_5bbef48fa35b2

rule_constraints.invariant: seat_count is a positive integer within availability and total == seat_count * catalog_price
rule_constraints.precondition: order contains a paid add-on with a per-seat catalog price
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject mismatched totals, invalid counts, and composite price fields; decrement availability atomically

text: Security invariant: an OTP is delivered only through the out-of-band channel bound to the claimed number, is never present in any API response, log, or client-visible artifact, and is single-use and time-bound. Precondition: a caller requests verification for a subscriber number. Postcondition: the response contains only a reference identifier and generic status; verification succeeds only when the submitted code matches the server-stored hash for the same normalized number and has not expired or been consumed. Verification must not grant a broader session than the specific subscription action.

metadata.title: OTP Confidentiality and Subscriber-Bound Verification
metadata.report_title: OTP bypass - Unintended disclosure of OTP to client allows attacker to manage users' subscriptions

rule_constraints.invariant: otp absent from all client-visible responses and hash_equals(stored, submitted) for the same number
rule_constraints.precondition: a caller requests an OTP for a subscriber number
rule_constraints.postcondition: return no OTP value, and grant only the specific action after single-use verification

text: Security invariant: paid entitlements exist only while a settled invoice covers the current plan and seat count; failed payment, cancellation, and downgrade all revoke excess entitlements immediately. Precondition: an account changes plan, seat count, or billing state. Postcondition: the entitlement set equals the highest plan fully covered by settled payments, and any failure or cancellation reduces access to the free tier until settlement succeeds. Billing state changes must be driven by verified payment provider events, not by client navigation.

metadata.title: Entitlement Invariant Tied to Successful Payment
metadata.report_title: [app.lemlist.com] Improper handling of payment lead to bypass payment

rule_constraints.invariant: entitlements <= plan_covered_by_settled_invoices and cancellation revokes paid access
rule_constraints.precondition: account changes plan, seat count, or billing state
rule_constraints.postcondition: failed or cancelled payment leaves only free-tier access until a verified settlement occurs

text: Security invariant: a promotional offer is accepted at most once per entitled account, and the total credit applied never exceeds the offer value. Precondition: an account holds an unconsumed offer with a defined value. Postcondition: the acceptance handler atomically marks the offer consumed, writes exactly one credit entry keyed by offer identifier, and returns the existing result for duplicate requests. Concurrent requests must serialize on the offer record, not on a pre-read balance.

metadata.title: Single-Redemption Invariant for Promotional Fee Credits
metadata.report_title: Fee discounts can be redeemed many times, resulting in unlimited fee-free transactions

rule_constraints.invariant: applied_credit <= offer.value and offer.consumed transitions once
rule_constraints.precondition: account holds an unconsumed promotional offer
rule_constraints.postcondition: duplicate or concurrent acceptance returns the original result and creates no additional credit

text: Security invariant: every coupon has an explicit scope, expiry, and redemption cap, and each application atomically increments a redemption counter bound to the account and to the coupon. Precondition: a cart applies a coupon code. Postcondition: reject the coupon when the account or global cap is reached, when it has expired, or when it is not applicable to the cart; record the redemption with the order identifier. Coupons exposed in public disclosures must be revoked, not merely monitored.

metadata.title: Coupon Redemption Cap and Per-Account Usage Invariant
metadata.report_title: Unlimited Reuse of Coupon Code Allows Free Shipping on All Orders on a Merch Store

rule_constraints.invariant: redemptions(coupon, account) < cap and now < coupon.expiry and coupon.applicable(cart)
rule_constraints.precondition: a cart applies a promotional code
rule_constraints.postcondition: atomically increment redemptions and reject reuse beyond the cap or after expiry

text: Security invariant: review status and delivery status are server-owned fields advanced only by the review and billing systems after their preconditions are satisfied. Precondition: an advertiser creates or updates a campaign. Postcondition: the update schema accepts only presentational and targeting fields; any attempt to set review or delivery state is rejected or ignored, and delivery begins only after a recorded approval decision and a settled prepayment. Status changes must be emitted by the state machine, never inferred from the request.

metadata.title: Server-Owned Ad Review and Prepayment State Invariant
metadata.report_title: Able to approve admin approval and change effective status without adding payment details.

rule_constraints.invariant: admin_approval and effective_status are not client-writable and advance only through the server state machine
rule_constraints.precondition: advertiser creates or updates a campaign or ad
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject or ignore writes to review and delivery state; require recorded approval and settled prepayment

text: Security invariant: an invitation can be accepted only by an identity that has proven control of the invited address, and role assignment on acceptance is capped at the role the inviter is allowed to grant. Precondition: an invitation exists for a specific normalized email and role. Postcondition: acceptance requires a verified email or a single-use token delivered to that address, the token is bound to the invitation, and the resulting role equals the invited role and does not exceed the inviter's grant authority.

metadata.title: Verified-Recipient Invariant for Partner Invitations
metadata.report_title: Shopify Partners Invitation Process Allows Privilege Escalation Without Email Verification

rule_constraints.invariant: recipient.email_verified == True and invitation.token_valid and invited_role <= inviter.grant_authority
rule_constraints.precondition: an invitation exists for a normalized email address and role
rule_constraints.postcondition: grant only the invited role after proof of control of the invited address

text: Security invariant: the seat limit applies to the sum of active members and outstanding invitations, and every acceptance re-validates the plan quota atomically. Precondition: a workspace has a plan-defined seat cap and at least one pending invitation. Postcondition: an invitation can be issued only if active_members + pending_invitations < seat_cap, and acceptance fails when the cap has been reached since issuance. The check and the membership insert must be one transaction.

metadata.title: Seat-Count Invariant Covering Pending and Accepted Members
metadata.report_title: User Limit Bypass via Pending Invitations in Workspace System

rule_constraints.invariant: active_members + pending_invitations <= seat_cap at issuance and at acceptance
rule_constraints.precondition: workspace has a plan-defined seat cap
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject issuance and acceptance that would exceed the cap, checked atomically

text: Security invariant: the invitation endpoint verifies the caller's 2FA enrollment and session strength on the server before creating any invitation, independent of client-rendered state. Precondition: a team administrator attempts to invite a member. Postcondition: reject with 403 when the account has not enabled 2FA or when the session was not established with the required factor, and never accept a client-supplied boolean as evidence of enrollment. The check must be evaluated in the same transaction as invitation creation.

metadata.title: Server-Side 2FA Enforcement on Invitation Operations
metadata.report_title: 2FA requirement bypass when inviting team members

rule_constraints.invariant: account.two_factor_enabled == True at the server before invitation creation
rule_constraints.precondition: an administrator attempts to invite a team member
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject the invitation unless server-side 2FA state and session strength satisfy policy

text: Security invariant: every approval decision is bound to the exact content version the approver reviewed, and the binding is mandatory. Precondition: a file is pending approval and has a current version identifier. Postcondition: the server loads the current version itself, rejects the decision when the submitted etag is absent, empty, or does not match, and records the approved version in the audit trail. Absence of a binding value must fail closed with a 4xx response.

metadata.title: Mandatory Version Binding for Approval Decisions
metadata.report_title: Approval app's file-freshness check can be bypassed by omitting the etag parameter, allowing approval of unreviewed file changes

rule_constraints.invariant: etag_present and etag_matches_current_version before an approval decision is recorded
rule_constraints.precondition: a file is pending approval with a current version identifier
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject missing, empty, or mismatched etags and record the approved version in the audit log

text: Security invariant: a payment event transitions an order only after the gateway response is authenticated, the payment identifier and amount stored at checkout match the event, and the signature covers every security-relevant field including the order token. Precondition: an order was created with a stored payment request identifier and amount. Postcondition: invalid MAC, missing binding data, amount mismatch, or replay all leave the order unchanged and return an error; a valid event is applied once and recorded idempotently.

metadata.title: Webhook Authentication and Payment-to-Order Binding Invariant
metadata.report_title: Instamojo CampTix: fail-open MAC + webhook Credit without binding payment to order

rule_constraints.invariant: valid_mac and event.payment_request_id == order.stored_id and event.amount == order.amount and not replayed
rule_constraints.precondition: order created with stored payment request id and amount
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject invalid MAC or mismatched binding without changing status; apply each valid event once

text: Security invariant: a session is marked authenticated only after every required factor succeeds, and the server stores that state rather than inferring it from cookie presence. Precondition: a password authentication step succeeds for an account with 2FA enabled. Postcondition: the issued session is explicitly partial, grants access only to the verification endpoints, and becomes fully authenticated only when a valid unexpired OTP is verified; deleting or modifying any cookie cannot promote it. Partial sessions expire quickly and are invalidated on failure.

metadata.title: Two-Factor Completion Invariant Bound to the Server Session
metadata.report_title: Email OTP/2FA Bypass

rule_constraints.invariant: session.auth_level == 'full' only after server-side OTP verification
rule_constraints.precondition: password authentication succeeds for a 2FA-enabled account
rule_constraints.postcondition: partial session accesses only verification endpoints; cookie deletion cannot change auth_level

text: Security invariant: fees are computed on the exact award amount and accumulated at full precision, with rounding applied only to the final invoice, and no award is accepted below a minimum that covers the smallest fee unit. Precondition: a program sets or repeats a monetary award. Postcondition: the total fee equals the configured percentage of the total awarded within one final-rounding unit, and micro-awards below the minimum are rejected. Metrics must reconcile awards and fees continuously.

metadata.title: Fee Computation and Rounding Invariant for Monetary Awards
metadata.report_title: Rounding errors on rewarding a bounty leads to bypassing the 20% H1 commission fee

rule_constraints.invariant: total_fee == round(final_sum(awards) * fee_rate) and award >= minimum_fee_covering_award
rule_constraints.precondition: a program sets or repeats a monetary award
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject awards below the minimum and accumulate fees at full precision before rounding
